Let <MATH_0001> be a quasi-compact morphism of schemes.
Then <MATH_0002> is closed if and only if specializations lift
along <MATH_0003>, see
Topology, Definition <REF_0001>.

According to
Topology, Lemma <REF_0001>
if <MATH_0001> is closed then specializations lift along <MATH_0002>.
Conversely, suppose that specializations lift along <MATH_0003>.
Let <MATH_0004> be a closed subset. We may think of <MATH_0005>
as a scheme with the reduced induced scheme structure, see
Definition <REF_0002>.
Since <MATH_0006> is closed the restriction
of <MATH_0007> to <MATH_0008> is still quasi-compact. Moreover specializations lift
along <MATH_0009> as well,
see Topology, Lemma <REF_0003>.
Hence it suffices to prove <MATH_0010> is closed if specializations lift along <MATH_0011>.
In particular <MATH_0012> is stable under specializations, see
Topology, Lemma <REF_0004>.
Thus <MATH_0013> is closed by
Lemma <REF_0005>.
